shorts.title: The Four-Word Pause
shorts.viewer_job: Reveal what the owner's stopped answer exposes, then reserve the practice and economic test for EP007.
shorts.hook_line: A buyer asks one last question. Four words into the answer, the owner stops.
shorts.spoken_copy: A buyer asks one last question. Four words into the answer, the owner stops. What happens here if you're gone for a month? The numbers looked good. But that pause opens a different question. Is the buyer getting a business, or a job only the owner knows how to do? There may be a one-person practice hiding inside that pause. I built the model. One unmeasured number decides whether it works. EP007 shows how to measure it.
shorts.short_payoff: The pause reveals that operating independence has not been demonstrated.
shorts.episode_gap: What service exists inside that failure, what it can honestly sell and how to test whether its economics work.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: One unmeasured number decides whether it works.
shorts.related_video_cta: EP007 builds the practice and shows how to measure that missing number. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.pinned_comment: EP007 builds the full sale-readiness practice, then shows how the first diagnostic should measure the number that decides whether the model works. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.visual_mechanism: An illustrative buyer question lands; four neutral answer marks appear and the trace stops. The one-month question fills the frame. The same operating task advances with the owner present and waits with the owner absent. The composition withholds the full diagnostic and resolves to an unmeasured hour count before the EP007 card.
claim_basis: script S00 buyer-owner cold open and one-month question
script S20/S21 modeled economics and unmeasured delivery hours
shorts.claim_boundary: The buyer-owner moment is an illustrative reconstruction based on the approved episode cold open. The visual shows only that independence has not been demonstrated. It does not claim a valuation effect, completed sale, proven demand, typical fee, known delivery hours or host transaction experience.

shorts.title: The Model That Fails Its Own Test
shorts.viewer_job: Show the base case missing its target, then reserve the two escape routes and decisive hour count for EP007.
shorts.hook_line: I gave this modeled one-person business eight clients at twelve thousand dollars each, and the base case still failed.
shorts.spoken_copy: I gave this modeled one-person business eight clients at twelve thousand dollars each, and the base case still failed. That is ninety-six thousand dollars gross. After modeled costs, eighty-six thousand remains before owner pay and taxes. My target was one hundred twenty thousand. The base case does not clear. This is not observed performance or an earnings forecast. Two escape routes remain, and both depend on delivery hours nobody has measured. EP007 shows how to measure them.
shorts.short_payoff: The published base case does not clear the host's target under its own modeled assumptions.
shorts.episode_gap: The two possible escape routes and the unmeasured delivery-hour assumption that decides whether either is credible.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: Two escape routes remain, and both depend on delivery hours nobody has measured.
shorts.related_video_cta: EP007 shows how to measure the missing hours. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.pinned_comment: These are modeled assumptions, not observed performance or an earnings forecast. EP007 shows both escape routes and how the first diagnostic should measure the missing hours behind them. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.visual_mechanism: Eight client records feed a gross-revenue counter; modeled costs subtract; the remaining contribution misses the target. The gap folds into a question mark rather than revealing either escape route.
shorts.claim_boundary: Every figure is a modeled scenario, not observed performance, typical pricing, attainable income or an earnings forecast. Delivery hours remain unmeasured.

shorts.title: The Part AI Cannot Compress
shorts.viewer_job: Separate compressible documentation from the human conversation and judgment that still control capacity.
shorts.hook_line: AI can compress the paperwork. It cannot compress the conversation this entire business depends on.
shorts.spoken_copy: AI can compress the paperwork. It cannot compress the conversation this entire business depends on. From a recorded interview, software can draft, organize and assemble. But someone still has to work out what a buyer will question, and tell the owner what only they know. The paperwork is compressible. The judgment is not. Nobody has measured that interview burden. EP007 shows why that missing number decides the model.
shorts.short_payoff: The documentation lane is compressible; the owner interview and accountable judgment remain human work.
shorts.episode_gap: How the unmeasured interview burden controls capacity and the practice's economics.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: Nobody has measured that interview burden.

shorts.pinned_comment: EP007 separates the AI work, the human work and the unmeasured interview burden between them. Tap EP007 under the channel name.

shorts.title: The Empty Seat
shorts.viewer_job: Rewind from the transaction to the early preparation work that has no clear compensated owner.
shorts.hook_line: The broker is paid by the transaction. Now rewind three years.
shorts.spoken_copy: The broker is paid by the transaction. The lawyer and accountant work at the deal. The wealth adviser enters when there are proceeds. Now rewind three years. No buyer. No deadline. No transaction. But the preparation work already exists. The episode's thesis is that this early work has no clear owner. That empty seat may be a business. EP007 builds it, then names what could make it fail.
shorts.short_payoff: The compensation structure around a transaction leaves an earlier preparation role unresolved in the episode's thesis.
shorts.episode_gap: What occupies the role, the bounded offer it can deliver and why the opportunity may fail.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: That empty seat may be a business.
shorts.related_video_cta: EP007 builds it, then names what could make it fail. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.pinned_comment: EP007 builds the practice that could sit in the empty seat, defines the demand test and models the economics that could end it. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.visual_mechanism: A closing table rewinds. Broker, lawyer, accountant and wealth adviser records disappear as the timeline moves earlier, but the preparation work remains around one empty chair.
shorts.claim_boundary: This is the episode's incentive-structure synthesis, not a market survey, universal compensation rule or criticism of individual professionals.

shorts.title: The Price That Changes the Job
shorts.viewer_job: Expose why the tempting success-fee route can cross into a different regulated role.
shorts.hook_line: The most tempting way to price this service may turn it into a different, regulated job.
shorts.spoken_copy: The most tempting way to price this service is a share of the sale. It may also turn the work into a different, regulated job. Preparation and brokerage are not the same thing. The boundary depends on the state, so this is not legal advice. If the success fee crosses that line, what can the operator honestly sell instead? EP007 builds the bounded offer and asks if its fixed-fee math survives.
shorts.short_payoff: A percentage-of-sale fee may move preparation work across a state-dependent regulatory boundary.
shorts.episode_gap: The bounded deliverable, fixed-fee structure and economics created by that perimeter.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: What can the operator honestly sell instead?
shorts.related_video_cta: EP007 builds the bounded offer and tests its modeled math. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.pinned_comment: Preparation and brokerage are different jobs, and the boundary varies by state. EP007 builds the fixed-fee alternative without giving legal advice. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.visual_mechanism: One invoice forks into fixed fee and share of sale. The percentage route crosses a hard perimeter and changes labels; the fixed-fee route stays unresolved and points into EP007.
shorts.claim_boundary: State-dependent and directional. Name no state, give no legal advice and tell viewers to verify their own jurisdiction.

shorts.title: A Real Problem With No Deadline
shorts.viewer_job: Separate agreement with the problem from willingness to pay before an exit is scheduled.
shorts.hook_line: An owner can agree this work matters and still never pay to do it.
shorts.spoken_copy: An owner can agree this work matters and still never pay to do it. An audit has a date. An inspection has a date. A possible sale three years from now does not. Agreement alone is not evidence of demand. The real test is whether anyone acts before the deadline exists. Two answers could end this business before the first invoice. EP007 identifies both.
shorts.short_payoff: A distant possible exit lacks the forcing function that scheduled audits and inspections have.
shorts.episode_gap: The two local answers that would falsify the opportunity and stop the build.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: Two answers could end this business before the first invoice.
shorts.related_video_cta: EP007 identifies both. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.pinned_comment: Owner agreement is not demand. EP007 identifies the two answers that should stop the build before the first invoice. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.visual_mechanism: Audit and inspection dates lock onto a calendar while a possible exit keeps sliding into an undated future. Two unlabeled stop gates appear before an invoice can form.
shorts.claim_boundary: Demand remains unknown. Do not manufacture urgency or imply that owner agreement predicts purchase.

shorts.title: Buyers Everywhere, Sales Nowhere
shorts.viewer_job: Use the market contradiction to open the question of what a buyer can actually inspect.
shorts.hook_line: Some small businesses attract multiple buyers while most listings never close. How can both be true?
shorts.spoken_copy: Some small businesses attract multiple buyers while most listings never close. How can both be true? One adviser survey says nearly nine in ten deals above five million dollars drew at least three offers. A separate industry estimate says only about three in ten listings close. Both figures are directional, not audited transaction data. But the contradiction points to a sharper question. If buyers exist, what makes one company inspectable and another too hard to trust? EP007 follows that missing layer.
shorts.short_payoff: Buyer competition in one reported subset can coexist with a low estimated listing-close rate across the broader market.
shorts.episode_gap: The preparation layer a buyer needs to inspect and the practice built around it.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: What makes one company inspectable and another too hard to trust?
shorts.related_video_cta: EP007 follows that missing layer. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.pinned_comment: The offer and close-rate figures are directional and come from different sources. EP007 follows the preparation layer between buyer interest and an inspectable business. Tap EP007 under the channel name.
shorts.visual_mechanism: Offer cards converge on one company while a larger field of listings falls away. Both resolve into a missing inspectable record rather than a causal claim.
shorts.claim_boundary: Both figures are directional and come from different populations. The adviser-reported offer result concerns deals above five million dollars and is not audited transaction data. Do not imply that preparation causes a close.

shorts.title: The Free First Customer
shorts.viewer_job: Turn a zero-dollar pilot into the hour measurement the research could not supply.
shorts.hook_line: The first version of this service should cost zero dollars. Not because free work proves demand.
shorts.spoken_copy: The first version of this service should cost zero dollars. Not because free work proves demand. It does not. The payment is a number the research could not produce: the real hours spent interviewing, cleaning records, writing and following up. A zero-dollar invoice becomes a stopwatch. That stopwatch decides whether the fixed-fee model can work. EP007 shows what to measure and what result should stop the build.
shorts.short_payoff: A free diagnostic can buy a delivery-time measurement, but it does not establish demand.
shorts.episode_gap: What the diagnostic must measure and what result should stop the fixed-fee model.
